why: KV-AHUB3 10-19 (LEAD2-KV, tree K.STA.AHUB): the SAFE attention hub as a LANDED-REGION parent. Both single-root SAFE kits failed the clock rule (sfa pin-flop spread 86.5 TT / 97.3 FF, sfb 116.3 / 123.2): one insertion-aware spine over 734.4 x 540 um padded every hub flop to the hard children's insertion (ot_nhb_zh 246.5, ot_qkh_recip_leaf 238.7). Regions: c = io / core / pin flops / relays / reciprocal leaf (centre-right logic band), z0..z3 = one Z tree each (its macro + landing halves). The core <-> Z tree buses are a cross-region LOOP (the core commands each tree and collects its root), so schedule 'reference': every landing +3 edges, the reference is the flat parent with ZW_RLY = ZR_RLY = 3 (the sealed hub's own relay parameters) and the compiler moves HUB_RECIP / HUB_PUB +6 (Z_LAND 6 keeps the core's RECIP > Z_START + 77 + Z_RT calendar check on the same law).

bench.why_expr: before the first regular pass (cyc 2040) starts are issued on every edge while the FLAT reference core's regional reset is still low after the port reset rose (rst_f && !u_flat.u_core.rn[0]); the last one reaches the core on its first released edge + 1, so a landed core whose reset run is one stage long (MUT 4) misses every start and runs no pass while the reference runs one (outputs diverge); later passes every 2000 edges exercise the Z trees and the reciprocal leaf
